headline: Shram Samvad: District Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes held in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh
content: A District Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme, “Shram Samvad”, on Labour Codes, Labour Welfare and Social Protection, was jointly organized by Ministry of Labour & Employment (MoLE), Government of India (GoI) and Labour Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh in collaboration with Association of Industries Madhya Pradesh and M/s Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd at Dewas, Madhya Pradesh on 5th November, 2026. The programme aimed at enhancing awareness among employers, HR, Legal and Finance professionals regarding the Labour Codes and rules made thereunder. It also focused on strengthening awareness and institutional capacity on labour reforms, welfare and social protection, promoting Centre-State coordination and stakeholder engagement. Shri S.R. Datta, Director, MoLE presided over the programme and participants included senior officials from MoLE, Labour Department, GoMP, Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) , Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) [CLC(C)], Directorate General Labour Welfare (DGLW) along with more than 100 participants from employers, industry representatives, legal, HR and finance professionals. The programme featured a series of technical sessions designed to provide participants with practical insights into the Labour Codes, employer obligations, and key social security initiatives of the GoI. Shri S.R. Datta, Director, MoLE presented the keynote address highlighting the key features of the Labour Codes. Various sessions were conducted by officials from MoLE, focusing on the key compliance requirements for employers under each of the four Labour Codes and Central Rules notified under the Labour Codes. The sessions provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, enabling participants to better understand the operational aspects of the new labour codes. Representatives from EPFO and DGLW also led sessions on Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme, respectively. To facilitate the employers and compliance professionals in effective implementation of the Labour Codes and Rules, ‘Handbook of Compliance for Employers’ and ‘Compilation of Frequently Asked Questions’ developed by MoLE were also shared with the participants.

headline: DA hike: Uttarakhand increases dearness allowance by 3% to 63% for state employees, pensioners — All we know
content: DA hike news: The Uttarakhand government has this week approved a 3% hike in dearness allowance for state government employees, increasing the component to 63% of basic pay, with effect from 1 July 2026, ANI reported.In a statement, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami's Office said this follows the Centre's own 3% DA hike to 63%, effective from July, announced in October, under the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC). The decision brings Uttarakhand state employees' DA at par with their central government counterparts, it added.Who benefits from Uttarakhand DA hike?Beneficiaries include the state government employees, eligible personnel working in local bodies, aided educational institutions, state universities, technical educational institutions, and those drawing salaries under the University Grants Commission (UGC) pay scales.The statement added that the differential amount, i.e. DA arrears, for the period from 1 July to 31 October 2026, will be paid in cash to eligible employees.DA helps to offset the impact of inflation on their cost of living for government employees. While Dearness Relief (DR), serves a similar purpose for pensioners by helping them manage the effect of rising prices on their pension income, the report added.DA hike announcements ahead of Diwali 2026DA is a percentage of employees' basic pay that aims to mitigate the impact of the rising cost of living and inflation. As per the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) recommendations, the Centre revises DA twice annually, using data from the All-India Consumer Price Index (AICPI).These announcements usually come in March and October, with rollouts in January and July. Effective from 1 July, the Centre's “Diwali gift” is the second DA increase this year, after it hiked the component by 2% in April from 58% to 60%, effective from 1 January for more than 1 crore beneficiaries — approximately 48.54 lakh central government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners across the country.Notably, besides the Finance Ministry's announcement on 28 October, state governments also hiked DA for employees and pensioners ahead of Diwali, adding ₹10,016.10 crore to the government's expenditure.This includes a 5% hike by the Himachal Pradesh government, 3% DA hikes each by the Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Punjab, Arunachal Pradesh and Gujarat governments, 2.5% increase by the Karnataka government, and 2% increases by the Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Kerala governments.Earlier this year, after the Centre's April announcement, the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) revised the DA and DR for employees for May, June and July 2026. Later, the Indian Railways also announced a 2% hike in DA and DR for staff and pensioners. Further, several states also followed the DA and DR hike announcements, including Telangana, Sikkim, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Maharashtra, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.(With inputs from Agencies)

headline: Himachal Pradesh to set up first fish parlour in Bilaspur, offering live and fresh fish for sale | India News
content: To promote fish marketing in Bilaspur district and ensure fish availability for both residents and tourists, the Himachal Pradesh Fisheries Department will establish a 'Fish Parlour' in the district, officials said on Sunday.Operating in conjunction with the Himachal Pradesh Tourism Department's 'Lake View Cafe' near the Fisheries Awareness Centre near Bilaspur's ITI Chowk, the parlour will provide tourists an opportunity to try traditional Himachali fish dishes.Also Read: Over 3 lakh silver carp fish seeds stocked in Gobind Sagar ReservoirA team led by the Director-cum-Warden of Fisheries, Om Kant Thakur, inspected the proposed site, necessary infrastructure, and other arrangements required for setting up the Fish Parlour.For the first time, the parlour will provide consumers with the option to purchase live and fresh fish. Furthermore, in future, the facility could be developed into a structured sales hub for a variety of fishery products.Also Read: Himachal sees rise in reservoir fish productionThis will provide local fishermen and fisheries cooperative societies with an additional platform to market their produce.The Tourism Department's cafe is already operational on the first floor of the same building. The synergy between the Fish Parlour and the cafe will enable the provision of local and traditional Himachali dishes prepared from fresh fish to tourists and other visitors.Also Read: Himachal government extends support to fishermen with 70% subsidy on boats, 90% on fishing gearThe Fisheries Department's initiative is expected to boost fish consumption and marketing in the district, while also creating new employment and income opportunities. Furthermore, this will help increase the number of tourists and visitors at the Lake View Cafe.Through the collaborative efforts of the Fisheries Department and the Tourism Department, this initiative could give a new identity to local fishery products in Bilaspur and integrate Himachali fish-based culinary offerings with tourism activities.
